methodology.llvm_ir_instructions: lines in generated_<shape>.ll containing ' = ' or starting with store/br/ret/call, whole file (both the raw kernel and the _mlir_ciface_ wrapper -- unlike the Stage 1 artifact, this count is NOT split by symbol, since llvm-objdump does not cleanly separate the fully-inlined vectorized loop body from the wrapper at the instruction-mnemonic level the way it did for the unvectorized generic kernel)
methodology.aarch64_instructions: llvm-objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn on the whole .o, address-prefixed lines, mnemonic field only
methodology.vector_instructions: count of disassembled lines referencing an AArch64 SIMD/vector register (v0-v31, any width suffix: .4s/.2d/.16b/etc.)
methodology.fmla: count of disassembled lines whose mnemonic is exactly 'fmla' (fused multiply-accumulate, the NEON instruction LLVM selected for the vector.contract outerproduct lowering)

note: generic/ counts here reflect the corrected lowering (linalg.fill zero-init) and are 150 AArch64 instructions / 1768 bytes at every shape (+16 instructions / +64 bytes vs. the pre-fix Stage 1 baseline of 134 instructions / 1704 bytes -- the honest cost of the fix, see README.md). generic/ has zero vector instructions and zero fmla at every shape: it is a scalar loop nest by construction (transform-preload-library was never applied to it), so instruction/object size does not grow with M*N*K. vectorized/ is fully unrolled by transform.structured.vectorize_children_and_apply_patterns for these fixed static shapes, so its instruction count and object size scale with M*N*K (8x8x8 -> 32x32x32 is a 64x increase in MACs and roughly a 64x increase in vectorized AArch64 instruction count: 274 -> 28026).
